---
title: "05 — Closed-loop LIGO arm"
---

The most realistic case: a suspension in series with a Fabry–Pérot cavity,
measured **with the feedback loop closed**.

What the instrument sees is the closed-loop response
$$T = \frac{P}{1+PC}$$
not the open-loop plant `P`.  Fitting `T` and calling it the plant is *biased* —
the feedback suppresses the resonance in `T`, so a loop-ignorant fit understates
the plant gain near the resonance.  Knowing the controller `C`, we recover the
unbiased plant estimate:
$$\hat{P} = \frac{\hat{T}}{1 - \hat{T} \cdot C}$$

We use `python-control` (a dependency) for the series/feedback algebra, and the
package's `TFModel` + `InvfreqsEstimator` for the fit.

```{python}
import numpy as np
import plotly.graph_objects as go
import control as ct

from system_ident.model import TFModel
from system_ident.estimators.invfreqs import InvfreqsEstimator

def to_tfmodel(sys):
    """Convert a python-control TransferFunction to TFModel."""
    sys = ct.tf(sys)
    num = np.atleast_1d(np.asarray(sys.num[0][0], dtype=float))
    den = np.atleast_1d(np.asarray(sys.den[0][0], dtype=float))
    return TFModel(num=num, den=den)

# Open-loop plant: suspension (1 Hz, Q=20) × cavity pole (100 Hz)
wn, Q = 2 * np.pi * 1.0, 20.0
susp  = ct.tf([wn**2], [1, wn/Q, wn**2])      # DC gain = 1
wc    = 2 * np.pi * 100.0
cav   = ct.tf([wc], [1, wc])                  # DC gain = 1
P     = ct.minreal(susp * cav)

C     = ct.tf([2.0], [1.0])                   # proportional controller, gain = 2
T     = ct.minreal(ct.feedback(P, C))         # closed-loop

P_model = to_tfmodel(P)
T_model = to_tfmodel(T)
```

## Measure the closed loop and fit it

```{python}
freq  = np.logspace(-1, np.log10(50.0), 500)    # 0.1 .. 50 Hz
H_T   = T_model.eval(freq)
rng   = np.random.default_rng(0)
H_err  = np.abs(H_T) * 0.02
H_meas = H_T + (rng.standard_normal(freq.size) + 1j * rng.standard_normal(freq.size)) * H_err / np.sqrt(2)

prior = TFModel(num=T_model.num.copy(), den=T_model.den.copy())
T_hat = InvfreqsEstimator().fit(freq, H_meas, H_err, prior)
```

## Recover open-loop P by dividing out the controller

```{python}
T_hat_ct = ct.tf(list(T_hat.num), list(T_hat.den))
P_hat    = ct.minreal(T_hat_ct / (1 - T_hat_ct * C))
P_hat_model = to_tfmodel(P_hat)
```

```{python}
#| label: fig-closedloop
#| fig-cap: "Loop-ignorant fit overstates suppression near the resonance; controller-division recovers the true open-loop plant. Zoom in near 1 Hz to compare. Use the legend to toggle traces."

SKY  = '#1F8AC0'
GOLD = '#C8973A'
RED  = '#E53E3E'
GRAY = '#94A3B8'

fig = go.Figure()

fig.add_trace(go.Scatter(
    x=freq, y=np.abs(P_model.eval(freq)), mode='lines',
    line=dict(color=SKY, width=2.8),
    name='True open-loop plant P',
    hovertemplate='%{x:.3f} Hz   |P| = %{y:.5f}<extra></extra>',
))
fig.add_trace(go.Scatter(
    x=freq, y=np.abs(T_model.eval(freq)), mode='lines',
    line=dict(color=GRAY, width=1.8, dash='dot'),
    name='Closed-loop T  (biased — feedback suppresses resonance)',
    hovertemplate='%{x:.3f} Hz   |T| = %{y:.5f}<extra></extra>',
))
fig.add_trace(go.Scatter(
    x=freq, y=np.abs(P_hat_model.eval(freq)), mode='lines',
    line=dict(color=GOLD, width=2.2, dash='dash'),
    name='Recovered P̂  (controller-division)',
    hovertemplate='%{x:.3f} Hz   |P̂| = %{y:.5f}<extra></extra>',
))

# Annotate the resonance
idx_res = np.argmax(np.abs(P_model.eval(freq)))
fig.add_annotation(
    x=freq[idx_res], y=np.abs(P_model.eval(freq))[idx_res],
    text='<b>Resonance<br>suppressed in T</b>',
    showarrow=True, arrowhead=2, arrowsize=1.1,
    arrowcolor='rgba(148,163,184,0.7)',
    ax=-80, ay=30,
    font=dict(size=10, color=GRAY, family='Outfit, sans-serif'),
)

fig.update_layout(
    template='plotly_white', height=420,
    margin=dict(l=60, r=20, t=20, b=55),
    font=dict(family='Outfit, Inter, sans-serif', size=12),
    legend=dict(orientation='h', yanchor='bottom', y=1.02, xanchor='right', x=1,
                bgcolor='rgba(255,255,255,0.9)', bordercolor='#DCE5F0', borderwidth=1,
                font=dict(size=10)),
    xaxis=dict(title='Frequency  [Hz]', type='log', gridcolor='rgba(30,60,100,0.07)'),
    yaxis=dict(title='|G(f)|', type='log', gridcolor='rgba(30,60,100,0.07)'),
)
fig.show()
```

::: {.callout-important}
## The bias is significant

Near the 1 Hz resonance, the proportional controller with gain 2 suppresses
the closed-loop response by roughly `1/(1+PC)`.  A loop-ignorant estimator
reports a flat, well-behaved plant; the controller-division step reveals the
sharp resonant peak that was hidden.  At LIGO, where control gain can be 40 dB
or more near a pendulum resonance, the bias from loop-ignoring is severe.
:::

::: {.callout-tip}
## Future work: controller-aware estimator

The current workflow requires the operator to supply the controller `C` as a
known `python-control` object and perform the division manually after fitting.
A controller-aware estimator that folds `C` into the cost function — so the fit
directly targets `P` rather than `T` — is a natural extension.
See the design spec's "future work" section.
:::
